value.text: At source level, publishPending declares a fixed delay from PUBLISH_INTERVAL_MS with a 1000 ms default; runtime registration and activation are unverified. Each invocation opens a database transaction and selects at most one unpublished outbox row ordered by id with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. The query uses identifier order, not event-time order. An empty selection returns without sending. For a selected row, the method waits up to ten seconds for the Kafka send future on weather.forecast-updated, then updates published=true in the transaction callback. Exceptions are logged as PUBLISH_RETRY with the exception class, and the method has no in-body retry loop. Kafka send and database commit are separate effects, so a completed send followed by a transaction failure or crash can leave the row eligible for replay. The source does not establish exactly-once delivery or runtime success.
